rounds.fact: eBay started in 1995 as AuctionWeb, reportedly built to help the founder's fiancee trade Pez dispensers. By 1999 it was already a sprawling grid of category links and live auctions.
Epicurious launched in 1995 as one of the first major recipe websites, built from the archives of Condé Nast's food magazines like Gourmet and Bon Appétit.
Kickstarter launched in 2009 and popularized the all-or-nothing crowdfunding model, where projects only get funded if they hit their goal, a rule meant to protect backers.
eBaum's World built its early traffic on hosting viral videos and flash animations, and was frequently accused of re-uploading other creators' content without credit.
Firefox launched in 2004 as a leaner alternative to a bloated Netscape, and its 'Download Day' campaign set a Guinness World Record for most software downloads in 24 hours.
